claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
Selective laser melting can introduce controlled porosity into HfMoTaTiZr.
Introducing controlled porosity by SLM can reduce the density of HfMoTaTiZr.
SLM-introduced porosity can reduce density without sacrificing room-temperature mechanical properties.
SLM-introduced porosity can reduce density without sacrificing mechanical properties at temperatures up to 1000 °C.
The intervention will produce a porous microstructure with optimized pore size and pore distribution.
Controlled porosity lowers the alloy's overall density.
An optimized porous microstructure retains sufficient load-bearing cross-sectional area to preserve mechanical strength.
Solid-solution strengthening remains effective in porous SLM-processed HfMoTaTiZr.
Lattice-distortion strengthening remains effective in porous SLM-processed HfMoTaTiZr.
The predicted result is reduced density with only minimal loss of mechanical strength.
The proposed performance boundary covers room temperature through 1000 °C under tensile and compressive loading.
A tensile-strength reduction greater than 20% at room temperature or elevated temperature is defined as falsifying the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says mechanical properties will not be sacrificed, while the predicted outcome permits a minimal loss and the rejection rule implicitly accepts tensile-strength losses of up to 20%. These are materially different preservation standards.

The claimed loading boundary includes both tensile and compressive loading, but the proposed falsification experiment and rejection criterion assess tensile strength only, leaving the compressive-performance claim untested.
